title: Assamese cuisine
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
body:
Assamese cuisine is the food of Assam, centred on rice, fish, fresh greens and herbs, with light spicing rather than heavy gravies. It is known for khar (alkaline dishes), tenga (sour dishes), pitha (rice cakes) and Assam tea.

Staples and dishes

Rice is eaten at almost every meal, often with fish, duck, pork or chicken, and with leafy greens, bamboo shoot and local herbs. Masor tenga (sour fish curry) and khar made with banana stem ash water are signature dishes.

Sweets and tea

Pitha — rice cakes filled with coconut, sesame or jaggery — are made especially at Bihu. Assam tea, grown in the Brahmaputra Valley, is the drink served with them and with breakfast.
extra:
Non-vegetarian dishes

Assamese non-vegetarian cooking is built on fresh river fish, local duck and chicken, pork and goat, cooked with little oil and spice — the flavour comes from souring agents like tomato, elephant apple and fermented bamboo shoot, from black sesame, mustard greens and bamboo shoot, rather than heavy masala. Each dish below has its own article under the Assamese cuisine category.

Til Gahori, Khorisa Gahori, Ou Tenga Gahori, Gahori Lai Xaak, Gahori Lau, Hah Kumura, Hahor Mangxo, Kukura Mangxo, Khorisa Kukura, Kukura Ou Tenga, Sagoli Mangxo, Paro Mangxo, Koldil Paro Mangxo, Masor Tenga, Bilahi Maas, Rou Maasor Jhol, Ou Tenga Maas, Patot Diya Maas, Sorsori Maas, Pura Maas, Isa Maas, Kankra Curry, Konir Jhol and Poita Bhaat with Maas.
